displayedInputs.question:
What is the perimeter of trapezoid \(ABCD?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

How many distinct triangles can be drawn using three of the dots below as vertices?

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

Isosceles right triangle \(ABC\) encloses a semicircle of area \(2\pi.\) The circle has its center \(O\) on hypotenuse \(\overline{AB}\) and is tangent to sides \(\overline{AC}\) and \(\overline{BC}.\) What is the area of triangle \(ABC?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

A square with side length \(2\) and a circle share the same center. The total area of the regions that are inside the circle and outside the square is equal to the total area of the regions that are outside the circle and inside the square. What is the radius of the circle?

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

The \(8 \times 18\) rectangle \(ABCD\) is cut into two congruent hexagons, as shown, in such a way that the two hexagons can be repositioned without overlap to form a square. What is \(y?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

Rolly wishes to secure his dog with an \(8\)-foot rope to a square shed that is \(16\) feet on each side. His preliminary drawings are shown.

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

Which of these arrangements gives the dog the greater area to roam, and by how many square feet?

A number of linked rings, each \(1\) cm thick, are hanging on a peg. The top ring has an outside diameter of \(20\) cm. The outside diameter of each of the other rings is \(1\) cm less than that of the ring above it. The bottom ring has an outside diameter of \(3\) cm. What is the distance, in cm, from the top of the top ring to the bottom of the bottom ring?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

A circle of radius \(1\) is tangent to a circle of radius \(2.\) The sides of \(\triangle ABC\) are tangent to the circles as shown, and the sides \(AB\) and \(AC\) are congruent. What is the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

mappings.answerReason: The semicircle area gives πr²/2=2π, so r=2. The center is the hypotenuse midpoint and its distance from either leg is half a leg, so AC=BC=4. The triangle area is 4·4/2=8.

mappings.rationale: The outside diameters form an arithmetic sequence. The hanging length is their sum minus the vertical overlap at each link, which is twice the 1 cm ring thickness.
mappings.answerReason: There are 20−3+1=18 rings, whose diameters sum to 18(20+3)/2=207. The 17 links each reduce the combined length by 2 cm, so the distance is 207−2·17=173 cm.

mappings.rationale: Tangency puts both centers on the apex angle bisector, which is the isosceles triangle's altitude. External tangency fixes their separation; similarity or half-angle trigonometry then determines the height and base needed for the area.
mappings.answerReason: The center distances from A are in ratio 1:2 and differ by 1+2=3, so they are 3 and 6. The triangle's height is therefore 6+2=8. A tangent from A to the larger circle has length √(6²−2²)=4√2. Similar right triangles give half-base 8·2/(4√2)=2√2, so the area is 8·2√2=16√2.
